rejected.title: Brønsted-Lowry acids and bases
card: Acid
a substance that donates a proton (H⁺) to another substance. A proton here is a hydrogen ion.
Base
a substance that accepts a proton from another substance. Acid and base roles go together: one gives, the other receives.
In HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻, HCl donates a proton to H₂O. So HCl is the acid and H₂O is the base.
Polyprotic acid
an acid that can donate more than one proton per molecule. H₂SO₄ can donate two. H₃PO₄ can donate three.
rejected.remember: An acid gives a proton and a base takes it. Polyprotic acids can give more than one.

a.q: In the reaction NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻, which species acts as the acid?
opts: H₂O, because it donates a proton to NH₃
NH₃, because it donates a proton to H₂O
H₂O, because it accepts a proton from NH₃
NH₃, because it accepts a proton from H₂O
a.why: NH₃ becomes NH₄⁺, so it gains a proton and is the base. H₂O becomes OH⁻, so it loses a proton and is the acid. Water is not always the base: the role depends on whether it gives or takes the proton.
a.clue: Compare the formula of water before and after. Did it gain or lose an H?

b.q: Phosphoric acid, H₃PO₄, is used in some soft drinks. Which statement about it is correct?
opts: It can donate up to three protons per molecule
It can accept up to three protons per molecule
It can donate one proton, as it has one acidic atom
It can donate three protons, but only to a hydroxide ion
b.why: H₃PO₄ has three hydrogens that can be donated as protons, so it is polyprotic. It is an acid because it donates, not accepts. Its protons can be donated to any base, not only to hydroxide ions.
b.clue: Polyprotic means more than one proton can be given. Is an acid a giver or a taker?

problems.detail: NH₃ is a weak base and only partly reacts with water, so this reaction is properly written as an equilibrium (⇌), not with a one-way arrow (→). The one-way arrow could suggest ammonia reacts fully, which clashes with the strong and weak acids point later in the chapter.

a.q: In the reaction HNO₃ + NH₃ → NO₃⁻ + NH₄⁺, which species acts as the base?
opts: NH₃, because it accepts a proton from HNO₃
HNO₃, because it accepts a proton from NH₃
NH₃, because it donates a proton to HNO₃
HNO₃, because it donates a proton to NH₃
a.why: NH₃ becomes NH₄⁺, so it gains a proton and is the base. HNO₃ becomes NO₃⁻, so it loses a proton and is the acid. The tempting mistake is to call the larger or first-listed species the base: the role depends on whether a species gives or takes the proton.
a.clue: Compare the formula of NH₃ before and after. Did it gain or lose an H?
